The light emitted by a phosphor after excitation.
The mildly euphoric feeling experienced after a pleasurable experience, especially after an orgasm or drug-induced high.
An afterparty.
s.x: There's an afterglow with singing after the evening worship.

s.g: After opening hours, usually after midnight and before daybreak.
The hyperpolarizing phase of a neuron's action potential.
An image which persists or remains in negative after the original stimulation has ended.
A conscious existence after death; a supernatural life that follows one's natural life, in some worldviews.
s.x: Many religious people believe in an afterlife.

s.g: The place believed to be inhabited by people who have died.
s.x: You'll reunite later, somewhere in the afterlife.

s.g: (countable, uncountable, now chiefly informal) The part of a person's life that follows a particular stage or event; later life.
s.x: They say that life begins at 40, but right now I'm more interested in the afterlife that begins at 65!

s.g: The effects of a person's actions, or their reputation, after death.
s.x: The philanthropic endowment that she bequeathed gave her an ongoing afterlife.

s.g: The events or situations that result from a particular event; the later reception, consumption or reworking of something, especially a cultural production such as a film, book, etc.
s.x: The 1970s TV show M*A*S*H had a long afterlife in syndication.

s.g: Light that follows something, especially the dim light in the sky after the sun has fully set.
(physiology) The load on a working muscle from a constant opposing force
(business) The market for further goods and services, such as replacement parts and accessories, subsequent to the sale of a product such as an automobile or computer.
(business) The industry that serves that market.
(finance) Trading activity in a security immediately following its initial offering to the public.
(business) To sell goods or services in the aftermarket.
That which happens after, that which follows, usually of strongly negative connotation in most contexts, implying a preceding catastrophe.
s.x: In contrast to most projections of the aftermath of nuclear war, in this there is no rioting or looting.

s.g: (obsolete, agriculture) A second mowing; the grass which grows after the first crop of hay in the same season.
The part of the day from noon or lunchtime until sunset, evening, or suppertime or 6pm.
(figuratively) The later part of anything, often with implications of decline.
(informal) A party or social event held in the afternoon.
(archaic in the singular) In the afternoon.
Every afternoon.
s.x: We are closed afternoons.

s.g: (now chiefly historical) An additional work following the main work; especially, a minor entertainment performed after a play.
(nautical) The heel of a rudder.
(UK, Ireland, informal, uncountable) Dessert.
s.x: What are we having for afters, Mum? I really want ice cream.

s.g: (informal) The festivities held after a wedding meal.
s.x: To keep costs down at our wedding, we only had family at the banquet, but invited all our friends to the afters.

s.g: (UK, Ireland, informal, sports) Fighting or arguing off the ball or when play has stopped.
(UK, Ireland) An after-hours drinking session in a public house.
After-school care service.
(business) After the sale of a product.
s.x: Aftersale services are services, such as repairs, offered to a customer after the customer's purchase of a product.

s.g: Taking place immediately after school classes.
Of or pertaining to a program intended to care for and educate children in the time immediately after school classes.
a lotion, gel, or liquid used after finishing shaving
(seismology) An earthquake that follows in the same vicinity as another, usually larger, earthquake (the "mainshock").
(figuratively) By extension, any result or consequence following a major event.
Emotional and physical distress following a traumatic event.
Occurring after a show.
An event which takes place following a show
(television) A talk show that discusses another television show that has already aired.
Describing a cooling or moisturizing lotion applied to the skin after exposure to the sun, especially to soothe sunburn.
s.x: Apply aftersun lotion to avoid peeling and flaking caused by sun damage.

s.g: A lotion of this kind.
s.x: Put some aftersun on when you get home.

s.g: A taste of something that persists when it is no longer present.
The persistence of the taste of something no longer present.
s.x: Many people think certain artificial sweeteners have an unpleasant aftertaste.

s.g: (of wine) finish.
To think about after the fact, reflect on.
To repent, or feel remorse for; to regret.
A reflection after an act; a later or subsequent thought, action, or expedient.
s.x: She packed her sandals only as an afterthought, but she was glad she did.

s.g: Something additional to the original plan or concept.
s.x: This whole remodeling was an afterthought; we were only going to paint and call it good.

s.g: (very rare except in the past tense, possibly nonstandard) To expound as an afterthought.

afterthought.f: simple past and past participle of afterthink

s.g: (music, uncountable) Pressure sensitivity on an electronic synthesizer, allowing the musician to change the tone or sound of a note after it is struck.

(rare) A touch (feature or characteristic) added finally or as an afterthought.
A treatment applied after some other process.
(temporal location) At a later or succeeding time; after that;
an epilogue.
(of a letter) a postscript.
(to a book) an appendix.
A supposed world that is entered after death; the realm of the afterlife.
(politics, chiefly used by libertarians) used aggressively towards leftist and statist views as a form of get out!
